transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Wu (CTO - Sapphire Payments), Rita Gomez (Platform Eng), Noah Price (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
- Discovery focused on latency + throughput targets (p95 targets, concurrency), streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, and benchmarking plan.
- Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) with compliance constraints (SOC2, KMS).
- Next: benchmark run, pricing sheet, security docs.

Topics: p95 SLOs; concurrency and burst patterns; streaming and token/sec; batching and caching; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; security/KMS/SAML; benchmarking plan

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:12] Ethan: Hey, Ethan here, CTO, we own infra and platform at Sapphire. Rita and Noah are with me.
[00:18] Rita: hi all, Rita platform eng, we'll run the tests.
[00:22] Noah: Noah, SRE; focused on SLOs and incident runbooks.
[00:27] Jordan: great. Maya is our systems SE, she'll cover latency/throughput and benchmarks.
[00:30] Maya: hey all. quick agenda: understand your p95 goals, concurrency, streaming needs, any compliance gating, then propose bench plan.

[02:05] Ethan: our big ask - on payment flows we need p95 under 300ms for short prompts (single-turn auth/score) and for chat like experiences p95 under 600ms with streaming acceptable. We target 200 requests/sec typical and bursts to 1k qps during peak promos.
[02:45] Jordan: ok notable. is 200 rps overall or per-region?
[02:52] Ethan: per-region, mostly NA, EU as secondary.

[04:00] Rita: also data sensitivity - we need SOC2, KMS integration and the option for VPC/private deployment. We are considering hosted for speed but need dedicated or private for compliance.
[04:20] Maya: makes sense; we frequently see customers do hosted for initial eval then shift to Dedicated or Private for guarantees and compliance. For strict p95 SLOs dedicated pools + reserved capacity help a lot.

[06:10] Noah: curious about streaming: does streaming actually reduce p95 for perceived latency? we care about time-to-first-byte.
[06:25] Maya: yes streaming improves TTFB; you get partial tokens quicker. For p95 on end-to-end completion you still need compute headroom. Example: on our Dedicated 80-token short completion we often hit TTFB ~70-120ms and full completion p95 ~200-300ms depending on model and quantization. (note: rough numbers)

[08:05] Ethan: token/sec metrics — what can we expect tokens/sec per instance? we plan to benchmark with 512 token responses, mix of short and long.
[08:20] Maya: tokens/sec is model and hw dependent; for a 13B-ish open model on v100/A100-like GPUs we commonly see ~700-1500 tokens/sec per GPU in optimized runs, less if you enable high-quality int8 quant or longer context. With batching and KV cache reuse across calls you can drive up effective tokens/sec.

[10:00] Jordan: tradeoff is often latency vs cost. do you have a target unit cost?
[10:08] Ethan: unit cost target is tight; we need to keep per-1k token cost under a threshold. We'll evaluate.

[11:30] Rita: in terms of concurrency what does Redwood's routing do? if we hit 1k qps can you auto-scale fast enough?
[11:45] Maya: on Hosted we have autoscaling and smart routing across regions and model variants; scaling is fast but burst capacity may be throttled by cold-starts. On Dedicated you reserve pools and configure autoscale with burst capacity so you get more predictable throughput. For private/on-prem you control autoscale.

[13:10] Noah: any limits around streaming concurrency?
[13:20] Maya: streaming increases open connection counts but per-connection CPU is small. We recommend running dedicated pools for high concurrent streaming to avoid head-of-line blocking. Also prefix/KV caching helps when many similar prompts come in.

[15:00] Ethan: can we run a token/sec benchmark? we'd like an apples-to-apples for hosted vs our dedicated estimate.
[15:08] Jordan: yes, propose a 1-hour benchmark with your sample prompt set and synthetic burst pattern, we'll run both hosted test and a Dedicated config estimate.

[17:00] Rita: what's the instrumentation we get? we need p95 token latency metrics, per-route traces, token-level cost.
[17:15] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-model and per-route dashboards, traces; can export logs for auditing. We'll share docs.

[19:30] Ethan: security - KMS, SSO, RBAC. For private deployment we need HSM-backed keys and audit logs.
[19:46] Jordan: we support customer-managed KMS, bring-your-own key (BYOK) for Private, and our Hosted integrates with cloud KMS. SOC2 cert is available, we'll send the pack.

[22:00] Noah: curious about quantization: does int8/save quant impact latency and quality?
[22:15] Maya: int8/4-bit quant reduces memory and improves throughput per GPU — so lower latency under high concurrency — but quality regressions can appear. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profile per workload and runs small evals to validate.

[24:40] Rita: what about fallback policies if a model variant is overloaded?
[24:48] Maya: smart routing can fallback to a compatible but cheaper variant; you can configure automatic fallback to a shorter-context or lower-precision model to maintain availability.

[26:00] Ethan: for benchmarking: we want p95, median, p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens for each scenario.
[26:12] Jordan: agreed, we'll produce a bench report including p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost delta hosted vs dedicated.

[28:30] Rita: sample traffic: 70% short auth prompts (~30 tokens), 25% mid (~150 tokens), 5% long (500+ tokens). concurrency distribution: steady 200 rps ramp to 1k qps for 5-10 minute bursts.

[30:10] Maya: good to capture. For the burst pattern we recommend configuring dedicated pool with reserve for burst or enabling burst capacity on Hosted but be aware of potential cold starts. We can run the synthetic traffic with a 5min ramp and a 10min peak to measure p95 under pressure.

[32:00] Ethan: do you provide tooling for token counting and replay?
[32:06] Maya: yes we will provide scripts to replay and token-count; we'll also accept your prompt set. We'll run both streaming and non-streaming variants; streaming typically improves time-to-first-token but total end-to-end may be similar.

[34:15] Jordan: quick note on SLA: Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per plan. We'll attach SLA doc.

[36:10] Rita: excellent. about networking — for Private we need VPC peering and private control plane.
[36:20] Jordan: confirmed, Private uses customer VPC, optional on-prem package; we'll share topology docs.

[38:00] Noah: any suggested concurrency per GPU guidance? we often see SEs recommending N concurrent streams per GPU depending on model size.
[38:15] Maya: rough guidance: smaller models (<=13B) can handle higher concurrency, e.g., 16-64 concurrent short requests depending on tokens; larger models need fewer concurrent. But kernel and batching optimizations change this. We'll recommend a config after initial bench.

[40:45] Ethan: can you point to examples where customers achieved sub-300ms p95 on short prompts?
[40:55] Maya: yes we have benchmark notes — some payments customers on Dedicated 13B-ish setups with int8 and aggressive batching/low-latency kernels hit p95 ~220-320ms on short completions. We'll send the reference diagonal. (transcription: "reference diag" -> "reference doc")

[43:10] Jordan: ok wrap up — recap next steps.
[43:20] Jordan: we will: 1) send pricing + hosted vs dedicated sheet, 2) send SOC2/KMS docs and topology, 3) SE to prepare benchmark scripts and run hosted test with your prompt set, 4) schedule 1h bench session Sep 3.
[43:40] Ethan: sounds good. Rita and Noah, anything to add?
[43:46] Rita: just we'll send prompt set and token targets by end of day tomorrow.
[43:52] Noah: we'll want the scripts in our CI to replay.
[44:00] Maya: we'll post scripts and a runbook template.
[44:10] Jordan: thanks everyone.

[47:30] Meeting end.
